issues.legal_issue: Land may be requisitioned for a public purpose that is permanent in character under a power authorizing requisition for any public purpose.
material_facts: An authority requisitioned privately owned land to establish a new village site and build houses for people whose homes had been destroyed or seriously damaged by floods.
Rehabilitation at a new site was urgently needed before the next monsoon, and the need for the land for that public purpose was undisputed.
The requisitioning law was temporary in duration, and the lower court considered that the new village site was a permanent purpose.
issues.conclusion: The power to requisition was not limited to temporary purposes. Requisition for the permanent public purpose of rehabilitating flood victims was not, on that ground, an abuse of or unjustified under the law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5(1) of the Bombay Land Requisition Act, 1948 authorizes requisition where the authority considers it necessary or expedient and the purpose is public; its words “any land for any public purpose” do not limit the purpose to one that is temporary. Section 4(5) defines requisition as taking possession of land or requiring it to be placed at the State Government’s disposal. Section 9 provides for restoration of the land to its owner as far as possible when it is released, but does not restrict the character of the purpose for which it may be requisitioned. The temporary life of the law and the nature of the purpose are distinct. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: requisition_order_appeal and requisition_law_covers_any_public_purpose and authority_considered_requisition_necessary_or_expedient and purpose_is_public and purpose_is_permanent

predicates.requisition_order_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an order requisitioning land.
predicates.requisition_law_covers_any_public_purpos: The law under which the land was requisitioned authorizes requisition for any public purpose.
predicates.authority_considered_requisition_necessa: The authority considered requisitioning the land necessary or expedient.
predicates.purpose_is_public: The land was requisitioned for a public purpose.
predicates.purpose_is_permanent: The public purpose for which the land was requisitioned was permanent in character.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a requisition order made under a law covering any public purpose, and the authority considered requisition necessary or expedient for a public purpose, a permanent character of that purpose does not prevent the requisition.

issues.legal_issue: Requisitioning land does not preclude later compulsory acquisition of the same land under a separate acquisition power.
material_facts: The land was first requisitioned for a public purpose.
The State later initiated compulsory acquisition proceedings in respect of the same land.
The laws providing for requisition and compulsory acquisition contained no provision making the exercise of one power prevent the exercise of the other.
issues.conclusion: Requisitioning the land did not exhaust or make incompatible the power to initiate compulsory acquisition proceedings later; the later proceedings did not, by themselves, establish an abuse of the requisition power.
issues.legal_principle: The Bombay Land Requisition Act and the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 contain no provision that makes action under one preclude action under the other. Part VI of the Land Acquisition Act provides for temporary occupation of certain land for a public purpose or a company, but does not establish an incompatibility between requisition and compulsory acquisition. The court cited no earlier cases on this issue.

predicates.requisition_acquisition_compatibility_ap: The proceeding is an appeal concerning whether requisition and later compulsory acquisition are compatible.
predicates.land_was_requisitioned: The land was requisitioned for a public purpose.
predicates.later_acquisition_was_initiated: The government later initiated compulsory acquisition proceedings for the same land.
predicates.laws_do_not_make_powers_mutually_exclusi: The laws governing the two powers do not provide that exercising one prevents exercising the other.

issues.definition: When land has been requisitioned, later compulsory acquisition is not precluded if the governing laws do not make the two powers mutually exclusive.
